assets.rationale: Canonical Phase-6 Medusa, Foundry, ghost-model, and harness-manifest skeleton kit. The repository policy requires agents to start here instead of recreating harnesses.
Campaign-specific harnesses are useful implementation examples but must not become global attack conclusions or be copied without rebinding.
Existing source-bound harness authoring and overlay mechanics should be used for KB adaptations rather than a parallel materialization layer.
Useful campaign evidence/model history, but target-specific and therefore not a reusable global KB primitive.
Existing base lifecycle recipes already cover readiness, deploy/configure, deposit/withdraw, reward accrual, privilege transitions, minOut, and zero-supply restart workflows.

assets.reason: No dedicated reusable historical-exploit incident/reproduction corpus exists on the scanned baseline under the v3 KB identity.
assets.rationale: K07-K14 must introduce the first evidence-backed incident and controlled/historical/generalized reproduction without pretending current campaign scripts are historical proof.
Existing deterministic vault fixture/workflow can seed controlled tests where topology fits, but it is not itself a historical exploit fixture.
Existing Phase-6 execution preflight is the canonical gate for Medusa/Foundry Phase-6 work.
Historical/full lifecycle Anvil work must reuse the existing fork preflight path and pinned-state checks.
Archive RPC identity/state and historical code-readiness helpers directly support future historical replay qualification.
Existing execution/result/disposition/schema machinery is the evidence normalization surface to extend rather than replace.
Existing trusted mutable-RPC and staged snapshot abstractions preserve fork identity and secret isolation for simulations.
Existing Medusa smoke execution is reusable qualification evidence for backend integration.
The repository policy makes the existing Anvil-backed runner authoritative for full mutable simulations; no parallel Anvil backend should be created.
Repository policy defines exactly one canonical execution workflow and one qualification workflow. Exploit cases must remain data/content, not per-exploit workflow definitions.
Existing runner manifest is the capability discovery surface for execution-plane integration.
Existing negative/regression tests encode useful failure signatures for future K21 failure-doctor integration.

Prior BoostHub/lifecycle campaign executions are useful recipe candidates and evidence examples, but they are campaign-specific and must be normalized into reusable recipes instead of imported as global truth.
